question.text: Scenario: Mr. Harish Gupta, aged 50, is a business owner with a net worth of Rs. 8 crore. He has Rs. 1 crore available for equity investment and is evaluating two options: Option A — Equity Mutual Fund (Direct Plan, Growth): Large & Mid-Cap Fund with expense ratio 0.75%, SEBI-mandated diversification (minimum 35% large-cap, 35% mid-cap), no minimum investment, exit load 1% if redeemed within 1 year, daily NAV disclosure, SEBI Mutual Fund Regulations apply. Option B — Discretionary Equity PMS: Minimum investment Rs. 50 lakh, fixed management fee 1.5% p.a., performance fee 20% of profits above 10% hurdle rate (no catch-up, high watermark applies), portfolio of 15-25 stocks customized to Harish's risk profile, Rs. 5 crore net worth of PMS provider, quarterly portfolio disclosure. Additional information: Harish is in the 30% income tax bracket. He expects a 5-year investment horizon. He wants concentrated, high-conviction stock picking rather than broad diversification. He has a separate emergency fund and does not need liquidity from this investment. Question 4 of 5: If Harish invests Rs. 1 crore in the equity-oriented mutual fund (STT as applicable) and it grows to Rs. 1.5 crore after more than 12 months, what is his LTCG tax liability upon full redemption? Assume he has no other eligible Section 112A long-term capital gains for the year and that surcharge and cess are excluded.

answer.text: Rs. 6,25,000 at 12.5% on the full Rs. 50 lakh gain (no exemption)
Rs. 6,09,375 (12.5% of Rs. 48,75,000, i.e., Rs. 50 lakh minus the Rs. 1.25 lakh annual exemption)

explanation.text: The Logic: Long-term capital gain = Rs. 1.5 crore - Rs. 1 crore = Rs. 50 lakh. The first Rs. 1.25 lakh of eligible LTCG on equity-oriented mutual funds is exempt in the year, so the taxable LTCG is Rs. 50 lakh - Rs. 1.25 lakh = Rs. 48.75 lakh. Tax at 12.5 percent of Rs. 48,75,000 is Rs. 6,09,375 (excluding surcharge and cess). The Trap: The Rs. 1.25 lakh exemption must be applied before computing the 12.5 percent tax; ignoring it overstates the liability, as in the option that simply multiplies the full Rs. 50 lakh by 12.5 percent. Note: The exemption is annual and applies in aggregate across eligible Section 112A long-term gains; this question assumes no such other gains for the year.
